## Fixed

- `dossier --vlm` no longer turns a name the page does not print into an
  `applicant`. On one test submission the vision pass reported an
  applicant on p15, a floor plan whose title block names only the design
  firm's director and designer. The name is nowhere on the page or in its
  text layer, and it made the `applicant` check `disagree`. A vision-read `owner` or
  `applicant` on a page with an Armenian text layer is now kept only when its
  surname or given name is in that text; a scan, which has no text to test, keeps what the
  model read.
- The vision prompt now asks for the words printed before an owner's or
  applicant's name (`facts[].label` in the answers file, optional). It states that
  a title block's Տնօրեն / ՆԳՃ / Նախագծեց / Ճարտարապետ are designers, never the
  applicant. An applicant whose label is not «Դիմող», «Պատվիրատու»,
  «Կառուցապատող» or «հայտատու» is dropped.

- The application form of a representative, «X-ի ներկայացուցիչ Y-ից», now
  names its principal X as the applicant, never the representative Y
  (six test submissions). A company's form, «"NAME"
  ՍՊԸ-ից», and a note's «Կառուցապատող - << NAME ՍՊԸ>> ի դեմս …» name the
  company. The client line «ՊԱՏՎԻՐԱՏՈՒ» takes a hyphen and «և» (e.g.
  «ՊԱՏՎԻՐԱՏՈՒ - Լ. Բալայան»), and its label must now be followed by a
  separator, so «պատվիրատուին սեփականության» no longer yields the applicant
  «ին սեփականության».
- A company owner or applicant is `org:` its legal form and name
  (`org:llc-nakhatip`), from the certificate, the form or a vision answer
  alike, so a company is compared with itself and never with its director.
- A page with no text that a binary labelled only `cad_drawing` (or
  `unknown`, `qr`) is `trust: unknown`, not `applicant`: every such page in the
  corpus is a Committee map extract nobody has read. `official_readability`
  now says those pages are unread rather than calling them official.

Answers files recorded before this release carry no labels and still merge,
tested only against the text layer. Re-merging one submission's recorded
answers drops that one fact and changes nothing else. Another submission's 21
vision facts and its three `signature` checks are unchanged. A fresh `--vlm` run
of three submissions reports no applicant outside a client or requester
line.

The reviewed dossiers 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10 are regenerated. Each gains its
applicant from the form or loses the fragment, and nothing else changes. The
scorecard baseline rises: facts 0.7391 → 0.7572, checks 0.7312 → 0.7485.
One ledger spelled its applicant's key differently from the toolkit's own
transliteration (as another ledger already had it). Across 20 external test
submissions, the only consistency outcome that changes is one submission's applicant,
`cannot_determine` → `compliant`, which is what its pages say.
